newsitem.title: USA: Florida low temperatures not too damaging - FASS.
newsitem.headline: Florida low temperatures not too damaging - FASS.

text.p: Freezing temperatures in the Florida citrus belt were not low enough for long enough to cause serious damage to citrus trees, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.
However, FASS said there was damage to new growth and fruit icing in many areas of the state.

According to FASS, most citrus groves were in very good condition before temperatures fell to as low as 19 degrees Fahrenheit in some areas, over the weekend. Harvest of early and mid oranges and the movement of fresh fruit was slowed slightly by wet conditions, FASS said.
Caretakers in the area are mowing, chopping, and discing cover crops. FASS said very few sprays and fertilizers were applied this week due to the adverse weather conditions.
FASS reported an estimated 266,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended January 19, up from 195,000 boxes the previous week and 222,000 boxes in the week ended January 5.
An estimated 11,053,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended January 19, up from 9,612,000 boxes the prior week and 9,808,000 boxes the week ended January 5.
